key_highlights: ASX volatile: banks, tech, and mining stocks fell on rising oil prices, while energy and select miners rallied intraday (#14, #51)
Iron ore in sustained downtrend pressuring BHP, RIO, FMG; BHP under severe earnings pressure (#19, #52)
RBA unlikely to cut rates to rescue property market; property sector faces 'GFC moment' (#58, #34)
Gold sector strong: Forrestania hits 2M oz, Kaiser restocks, Larvotto NSW strike, Aureka $8.9M acquisition (#40, #42, #43, #44)
Hormuz Strait escalation elevates oil/energy risk premium (#24)
Housing builders collapsing despite shortage; living standards under pressure from mortgage costs (#3, #6, #50)
Super policy debate intensifies with Treasury under political pressure (#20)
CPI data and 'Big Bond Scheme' week ahead for markets (#67, #69)

sectors.trend: Iron ore in structural decline ('drowning'); BHP under existential pressure. Gold counter-cyclical strength with multiple ASX juniors hitting milestones. Uranium exploration active (Infini, Canada).
sectors.implications: BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX face margin compression. Gold names (FOR.AX, KAE.AX, LAR.AX, AUK.AX) attract rotation flows. Diversify away from iron ore exposure.

sectors.trend: Big four banks (CBA, ANZ, NAB, WBC) fell on rising oil-driven inflation fears. RBA unlikely to ease, keeping NIMs compressed. Property credit risk rising.
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, ANZ.AX, NAB.AX, WBC.AX face headwinds from property stress and sticky rates. Super policy debate adds regulatory uncertainty.

sectors.trend: Santos (STO.AX) under pressure as gas cartel dynamics shift. Hormuz Strait escalation supports oil prices, benefiting energy names. Qantas jet incident minor.
sectors.implications: STO.AX, WDS.AX, WEL.AX benefit from oil spike but face gas price volatility. Geopolitical risk premium elevated.

sectors.trend: Property industry at 'GFC moment'; builders collapsing despite shortage. RBA won't intervene. Transport hub housing boom in Sydney offsets some weakness.
sectors.implications: REITs (GPW.AX, ICPS.AX) under pressure. Construction names (WBC.AX, CGW.AX) face demand destruction. Selective transport-hub plays may outperform.

sectors.trend: Healthcare barriers (waitlists, bulk billing) under political scrutiny. CSL.AX stable. Consumer staples pressured by living standards decline and second-job trend.
sectors.implications: CSL.AX, WES.AX, WOW.AX offer defensive positioning. Consumer discretionary under pressure from mortgage stress.

sectors.trend: Tech stocks fell with ASX. Stokes family retakes Seven Network control. AI/data centre capex (NVIDIA, Equinix) global theme continues.
sectors.implications: SWS.AX (Seven) governance shift. Global tech (NVDA, EQIX) supports ASX tech sentiment but local names lag.

key_themes: Iron ore structural decline vs gold counter-cyclical strength
RBA policy paralysis: won't cut for property, won't hike for inflation
Housing supply-demand mismatch: builders collapsing, shortage persists
Hormuz Strait geopolitical risk elevating energy prices
Living standards erosion: mortgage costs, second jobs, public sector boom masking decline
Super policy political pressure on Treasury
CPI and bond issuance week ahead
Tobacco tax political fight (cigarette seizures, vapes)

risk_assessment.mitigation: Reduce BHP.AX/RIO.AX/FMG.AX weightings; rotate into gold and energy
Underweight REITs and construction; monitor bank NPLs; RBA unlikely to intervene
Hedge with energy exposure (WDS.AX, WEL.AX); monitor AUD/USD
Position for sticky rates; favour dividend payers with rate resilience
Favour staples (WES.AX, WOW.AX) over discretionary; monitor retail sales data
Monitor Treasury announcements; assess impact on fund managers and banks

opportunities.rationale: Gold at record highs; multiple ASX juniors hitting milestones; safe-haven demand from Hormuz risk and Trump uncertainty

opportunities.recommendation: Tactical energy exposure on Hormuz risk
opportunities.rationale: Oil price spike from Strait escalation; Santos gas cartel break creates volatility trading opportunity
Living standards collapse and mortgage stress shift demand to essentials; WES/WOW resilient

defensive_moves.recommendation: Reduce iron ore / large-cap mining exposure
defensive_moves.rationale: Iron ore in structural decline; BHP under severe pressure; no near-term catalyst for reversal
GFC-level stress in property; builders collapsing; RBA won't rescue; credit risk building in banks
RBA inaction, oil spike, and global bond supply (hyperscaler bonds) pressure AUD and push rates higher

market_outlook.short_term: ASX likely range-bound to slightly lower. CPI data and bond issuance week create volatility. Iron ore weakness drags materials; energy offsets. Banks under pressure from property credit fears. Gold and staples provide relative strength. Hormuz escalation adds tail risk.
market_outlook.long_term: Structural headwinds from iron ore decline, property correction, and living standards erosion cap upside. Gold, energy, and healthcare offer relative outperformance. RBA policy paralysis prolongs uncertainty. Super policy changes may reshape financial sector dynamics. 6-12 month: cautious, selective.

Iron ore contract pricing next quarter (#19, #52)
US midterms impact on global risk appetite (#55)

Bank NPL and credit growth data
US midterms and Trump policy signals
